chunks: And from him, from al-Barqi, from Fudayl ibn 'Abd Rabbih, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from some of our companions, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him)
And enjoying (sexual intimacy) with the believing woman is superior in all states; he narrated that.
ai.seo_question: What is the status of intimacy with a believing woman in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* affirms the superiority of sexual intimacy with a believing woman, a ruling derived through the chain of the prominent narrator Hammad ibn Isa. In Shia jurisprudence, this highlights the spiritual merit (*fadilah*) of marital relations within the context of faith, distinguishing it from mere physical gratification. The mention of 'mithluhu' indicates this is a corroborating report, reinforcing the consensus on this specific aspect of marital ethics.
